title: Which angles correspond in a transversal figure?
description: A line crosses two lines and makes eight angles. Angles one and five sit in the same corner at the two crossings. The board uses this to name the partner of angles two, three and four. Keeko doubts that angle two goes with angle five.
teaching_notes: One idea: corresponding angles sit in the same corner at the two crossings. Watch for students who pair angles by the next number instead of the same corner.

source: In the transversal figure, 1, 2, 3, 4 are at the crossing with l and 5, 6, 7, 8 at the crossing with m, with 1 and 5 in the same corner. Name the corresponding angle of each of 2, 3 and 4.
video_script.why: The child learns to find the corresponding angle by looking for the same corner at the other crossing.
video_script.substitution: The book's own pairs of corresponding angles: one and five, two and six, three and seven, four and eight.
video_script.anchor: A line t crossing two lines l and m, with the angles one to four at l and five to eight at m, and angles one and five in the same corner.
video_script.wrong_answer: angle two goes with angle five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the next number is the partner.
video_script.payoff_line: Two goes with six, three goes with seven, and four goes with eight.

final_answer.spoken: two and six, three and seven, and four and eight

maths_rules: corresponding angles are in the same corner at the two crossings
1 and 5 are in the same corner, so they are corresponding angles
2 and 6 are in the same corner, 3 and 7 are in the same corner, 4 and 8 are in the same corner
the slip: the next number is not the same corner; 5 is in the corner of 1, not of 2
video_script.design: One figure stays on the stage. Each pair of angles lights up in its own colour as the board names it, in the same corner at each crossing.
